stem: A client with severe long-standing COPD develops jugular venous distention and peripheral edema from right-ventricular dysfunction related to pulmonary disease. Which condition is most consistent with these findings?

options.B: An isolated renal disorder unrelated to pulmonary disease.
options.D: Left-sided heart failure caused solely by systemic hypertension.

rationale: Cor pulmonale is alteration in right-ventricular structure or function caused by a primary respiratory-system disorder resulting in pulmonary hypertension. COPD is a common cause, and advanced findings can include jugular venous distention and peripheral edema. Therefore A is correct.
educational_objective: Recognize cor pulmonale as right-ventricular dysfunction associated with chronic pulmonary disease and pulmonary hypertension.
source_version_date: Last Update August 8, 2023; current StatPearls chapter rechecked 2026

source_claim_supported: Cor pulmonale is right-ventricular structural/functional impairment caused by primary respiratory disease with pulmonary hypertension; COPD is a common cause; JVD and peripheral edema may occur in advanced disease.

correction_summary: Removed the distracting conversational narrative, stated the pulmonary-disease/right-ventricular relationship precisely, and avoided implying that peripheral edema is specific by itself. Reduced difficulty from hard to easy.
audit_findings: NCBI StatPearls directly supports A. The final stem includes the defining pulmonary-disease/right-ventricular relationship rather than relying on nonspecific edema alone. Independent second pass passed.
